sections.h: CHRIST IN YOU

FOREWORD

“The Father willed to accomplish the redemption of men through the work of a «Poor One» who… fulfilled his mission without splendor, with gentleness and, apparently, with failure… He lived poor among the poor and addressed his teaching and his «good news» chiefly to the poor… and ended his earthly existence in the supreme humiliation and poverty of the cross” (Statute nos. 9 and 10).

This is the Christ who wished to share our human condition. A truly wretched condition, if destined to experience the drama of death!

We must not be deceived by the illusions of easy successes, nor led astray by the mirage of brilliant securities or seductive riches… Fundamentally we are… mortally wounded! Let us say it plainly: dying! We have seen it, meditating on the history of salvation, through Israel’s harsh pilgrimage. That people remains the model of every man who walks in search of a land…

Without God’s compassion, without his loving initiative, his interventions, his repeated promises of covenants, his oaths not to abandon this people, so fragile, unfaithful, stubborn, ungrateful, after all…all of us would be in despair, without salvation, with the only sure destiny of ending in loneliness, forgotten forever in a cemetery! Here is the deep meaning of our existence, without that God who revealed himself to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob… Whom all the oppressed, the discouraged, the poor of the earth awaited; who lifted up the “barren” woman from her humiliation, who made fruitful the womb of a “virgin” (…just think!), promising her…divine motherhood!

The face of this God has been manifested in his Christ: in that Jesus who, out of pure and free love, has drawn close to each one of us, showing on the cross the ugliness of our sin, but also the glory of the Only-Begotten Son of the Most High God!

“We proclaim your death, we proclaim your resurrection, until you come again”: so, in the Eucharistic celebration, we bear witness to the mystery of our faith!

It is true, we do not yet see, in all its splendor, the fullness of life and the lordship that Jesus today possesses “over death and Hades” (Rev 1:18), but we know and believe the testimony of the apostles, the presence of the Holy Spirit who “groans” in our hearts, enlightening and sustaining them with this consoling truth: “to him who loves us and has freed us from our sins by his blood, who has made us a kingdom of priests for his God and Father, to him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen” (Rev 1:5-6).

Still pilgrims, then, but with the eyes of faith turned on high… and committed here below as well to “searching” the Scriptures, because all of them speak of Him!

And already at the dawn of creation, Jesus was present…

Only the Scriptures draw him out of the concealment and humiliation to which our history still consigns him… The world would like to seal him in the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea and of Him… let there be no more talk!

But that original command: “Let there be light!” is the word that will burst resolutely into our darkness, into our tombs!…

That divine word is creative… “all things were made through it.”

That “light”… comes.

That “light”… enlightens every man.

That “light”… gives the power to become “children” of God.

That “light,” finally, “dwells” among us forever and is… the man Jesus!

Every page of Sacred Scripture sings and praises the journey of Jesus and we, “docile to the call,” celebrate the Word for this purpose: Jesus is “the Alpha and the Omega, who is, who was and who is to come, the Almighty” (Rev 1:8).

We want to discover the face of this “Poor One”; as the only one who has “served” humanity since the beginning.

The sheets, therefore, at the outset, will “glean” for a while at the roots of history, to show us the presence of this “Servant” of Yahweh who is already…a word of liberation!

❖ In Deuteronomy (as, after all, in the whole Old Testament), Israel will be invited to “listen.” To realize, that is, that there is a God who has loved him, who has concretely drawn near to his history of suffering. In short: liberation begins!

– “Listen!” will also be the joyful announcement that the apostles will proclaim throughout the world for the good news of another liberation, deeper than the one worked in Egypt. God, by raising Jesus, will free man from the slavery of sin, giving him forgiveness and communion with the Risen One.

❖ Listening in the wisdom books (see Proverbs) wants to free man’s heart from superficiality, from anxieties; to lead him to an adoring silence that discovers the presence of a God-Father and above all of a Wisdom-Bride.

– It is she, a concrete image of Jesus, who already shows us the divine desire to give himself, to serve man, to “delight” in our midst!…

❖ In the book of Sirach too wisdom is revealed as…a concrete person, who educates man to discover the beauty of God and to rejoice in the divine providence so solicitous for him.

– Jesus will exult in his spirit, revealing to us the greatness and goodness of the heavenly Father.

❖ Wisdom will also illuminate the drama of suffering (see Job), inviting man to prepare for temptation. In history an “enemy” is present…

– Jesus will openly reveal him and will “destroy him with the breath of his mouth” (2 Thess 2:8). Jesus will not…protest before humiliation and the cross. It is the true…wisdom, “divine, mysterious… hidden, which none of the rulers of this age understood…” (1 Cor 2:6-8).

❖ But what could they have known, had they only searched the book of Wisdom! A friend of man, she lets herself be found, she gives herself… She works in history giving strength, making her people glorious…every man!

– Is this not all that Jesus accomplished “in word and deed” in his earthly life?

A lover of life, he gives it “in abundance” still today, through his Spirit who animates and guides his Church.

“Apart from me you can do nothing,” Jesus will say to his own. And being unable to do anything shows itself in the path of man without God: a sad, inconsistent life… “vanity of vanities” every action of his, all his works. This is the bitter experience of Qoheleth!

“Rest,” on the other hand, Jesus the Bridegroom of a humanity precisely barren and in need of loving care and attention; “wandering” until it rests on the breast of him who loved it!

This encounter of salvation will be illuminated by the Song.

These “wisdom” celebrations will have the purpose of introducing us into the “knowledge” of the person of Jesus.

He, in fact, is far more than a LIBERATION; far more than a PATH OF SALVATION; more than CREATIVE WISDOM itself, lover of man, indulgent and compassionate towards him; more than the CONTEMPLATION of a benevolent God; far more than the victory over SUFFERING AND DEATH…

Jesus now shines in the inaccessible light of the Holy God, Holy, Holy…

Contemplating him as the “poor and suffering Servant,” however, we can, with him, through him and in him, be introduced into the very secrets of true wisdom: THE TRINITARIAN LIFE!

“Great beyond words is the most holy, infinite Triad, one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit… My Love! great mystery, oh, that I might be able to make you known to the whole world!… Oh, whoever comes to taste and possess that divine Essence, surely everything earthly serves him only as tedium! The intellect, opened by divine virtue, communicates with its immortal being and in that infinite sea of infinite greatness understands all, rejoices and delights in love” (Memoirs pp. 192-193).

Following Jesus on this path indicated to us by Fr. Sergio, we want to look, through the citations given at the end of each celebration, also at the discipleship of one of his followers, Blessed Anna Rosa Gattorno, to be encouraged and stimulated in this “adventure”…

Mother Rosa too let herself be “introduced” into the “knowledge” of the person of Jesus.

“Her deep experience, based on contemplation, undoubtedly has priority over the intellectual search for God. For her the revelation of Jesus: “GOD IS LOVE” (1 Jn 4:8) is not only a mystery of faith to be meditated on, it is above all an experience of love, the welcoming of a Presence dwelling in her being” (The Gift of God p. 79). “…I found in my Good true consolation and peace… My Eternal All, who can describe what you do and communicate to the soul and what it experiences in you. Today in you and you for me live, I feel I have no life but yours. You live for me. I feel a calm, an inner peace I cannot describe. How much strength he gave me; robust, as if I had done nothing…” (Memoirs p. 443)

“The sublime will of the Father to identify Rosa with his Beloved Son is manifested to her, in a special way, through the mystical experience with Jesus Crucified. She does not live in her life only the historical memory of the Crucified, but the dialogue with the glorious Jesus who lets himself be experienced by her in the mystery of the crucifixion.

It is a love encounter with him, from which she learns to give meaning not only to the joys and gifts she receives, but also to the sorrow of humanity and to her own sufferings. From Jesus she learns to love suffering as participation in his passion and ignominious death, perfect sacrifice and new and Eternal Covenant” (The Gift of God p. 43).

(The citations on Mother Rosa are indicative. Each person in charge may use, in this regard, the “material” at hand or ask for whatever is needed).

PART ONE

IF ONLY YOU WOULD LISTEN…

It is God’s lament over Israel, who had forgotten that it had an ally, a saving God committed to giving it not only existence, but fullness of life, happiness…

It is the concern of the “God of Sabaoth” in commanding that the great event of the people’s liberation from Egypt be told to future generations…

From the witness of the fathers, the new generations would learn to have faith in the God of Sinai, who is a fatherly “presence” for the whole nation…

We too can learn from the experience of the Old Testament that faith is born from listening to those who have “seen,” who were “present” at the wondrous events of the God who “loves life,” the “father” of all men…

…who “raised” Jesus of Nazareth, so that he might announce to all of us the “good news” of his victory over death and sin, but above all reveal to us his infinite mercy towards us, ungrateful and rebellious creatures…

CELEBRATION NO. 1

“HEAR, O ISRAEL”

(Gleaning from the Book of DEUTERONOMY)

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION

A question that often surfaces in our conscience, especially when we are visited by pain, loneliness, failure, the loss of something very dear that is torn away from us, is: “Why live… if I must suffer and die?”

A question, or rather a cry, that Israel surely asked in Egypt…

But God “heard” that cry (Ex 3:7.9.16-17)…

And Israel became a “spectator” (4:35; 6:22; 7:19; 10:21; 11:1-7) of an event: a God who comes out of silence, out of the… “hidden” (29:28), to have compassion (32:36) and to give life (32:47).

The event of this liberation sheds light on the happenings of history: these “revealed things are for us and for our children forever, that we may observe all the words of this law…” (29:28), so that Israel may be happy (4:40; 5:16.29.33; 6:3.18.24; 8:16; 12:25.28; 30:5.9) and live long (6:2).

The God whom Israel knows, in fact, “loves” his people (7:7-8) and “rejoices” in making them happy (30:9).

To forget, or not to pay attention to, or not to welcome this event is… to have one’s life “hanging by a thread,” to “find no relief” and no “place of rest”… “uprooted,” “scattered,” forced to serve despotic masters, to suffer “grievous and lasting diseases,” “a trembling heart, failing eyes and a languishing soul” (28:53-68).

Terrible will be this despair, which leads to destruction!

TO LISTEN (4; 5; 6:3-4; 9:1; 20:3) is therefore more than paying attention…

• it is: to remember (7:18)… to meditate (32:7)… not to forget (8:11-20)…

• it is: to inquire (4:32-33)…

• to call to mind (30:1) or to place in the mind (32:46)…

• to pitch camp at God’s feet to receive that word which makes saints (33:3)…

• to rejoice, celebrating the feasts of this liberation (16).

And Israel learns to… stop and listen, to… learn to act and to… hand on (6:6-9; 31:12-13). Like Adam of old, in fact, it receives a commandment for life (30:16)!

TO LISTEN will finally become a profession of faith, the witness of a way of life (26:1-9).

The importance of this “listening” makes God present in the life of Israel and makes this people a privileged nation, called to live in a “dialogue” that will never end; indeed, even in disobedience, through the breaking of the “covenant,” Israel will always be given the possibility of a rethinking, of a return (30:1-5).

We note, then, the importance of dialogue from the very first chapter:

– 1:6 God speaks

– 1:9 Moses speaks

– 1:14 Israel answers

– 1:16-17 the judges listen

– 1:17 Moses listens

– 1:27 the people murmur

– 1:34 the Lord listens

– 1:43 the people… do not listen

– 1:45 the Lord… does not listen

Reading: DEUTERONOMY 32:1-44

The “canticle” highlights the goodness of God, who chose this nation from among all (4:34), speaking to it from heaven (4:36), giving it a way of salvation (8:2-10).

God found Israel “in a desert land,” “encircled” it, “brought it up,” “guarded it as the apple of his eye,” “guided it alone,” “fed” it… But Israel “repaid” such divine predilection with rebellion and ingratitude…

There is so much bitterness in this song of Moses…

One wonders: could this have been the cause of the infidelity of Moses and Aaron, who did not show forth God’s holiness among the Israelites? (32:51)

– Did witnessing the people’s constant murmuring discourage them?

– Did they doubt the grace of God, who can always convert the heart of man, whatever slavery oppresses it?

– Or perhaps they did not accept that God could have chosen creatures so wretched and so insensitive to the beauty and wisdom of that Covenant?

– Were they then no longer able to walk on, their souls weighed down by pessimism, impatience, weariness? Did they too, therefore, stop at the threshold of the Land, in solidarity with the sin of Israel?

Moses’ words against Israel are very harsh: “foolish and senseless people” who “reject” and “despise” God, who “sacrifice to demons,” “senseless,” “stock of Sodom”; a people who forget… and who will therefore be even more rebellious after the death of Moses! (31:27)

❖ Perhaps God’s “holiness” lies in that “hoping against all hope” of his: that the people may at last welcome those “words”… and become the “only wise and understanding people” (4:6).

Otherwise, why speak to them “out of the fire” (4:12), why give himself to them, if afterwards, knowing the human heart (…which he created), he did not know it to be open to holiness?

Why communicate to them those sentiments of mercy, of profound attention to the smallest and the neediest (24)… if he had not trusted that Israel too could become sensitive to those appeals? “You shall remember that you were a slave” (24:22), “there shall be no one in need among you” (15:4).

Even in punishing, Israel must learn to be… “humane” (25:3), like its God, who does not take revenge, who is great and patient in forgiving, who extends his favor not only to those near but also to those far away (29:13-14).

PRAYER EXERCISE

Read all the citations attentively, a little each day…

Reading God’s word with respect is as if you were listening to his voice.

In fact, God, answering a request of the people, speaks to us through his prophets (18:15).

The Scriptures of the prophets are therefore inspired by the Holy Spirit; when you read… you listen to him who speaks to you: “today, do not harden your hearts!” (Psalm 95).

∼ ∼ ∼

• What have you understood of this importance of… listening?

• Do you really think that, despite the sin of the world and our personal frailties and temptations, all people are called to holiness?

• What can it mean for you today not to show forth God’s “holiness” among the people you live with (family, friends, work colleagues, schoolmates…)?

• How much importance do you give to the celebration of Christian feasts?

From Mother Rosa: “Travagli e conforti” p. 324

CELEBRATION NO. 2

LISTEN, MY SON!

(Gleaning from the Book of Proverbs)

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION:

The Book of Proverbs, too, asks for attention! To “know wisdom and discipline, to understand words of insight, to receive instruction in enlightened conduct… to give prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young” (1:1-4).

A pressing invitation to welcome God’s… “fatherhood”!

The inspired book, in fact, seems to want to call… man into the presence of the divine person of the Father, who lovingly leads him to the encounter with his Wisdom!

Certainly it is no accident that this wisdom, which precisely shows itself… personal, is presented in chapter 8, preceded by 7 (…the number of perfection!) fatherly appeals (…a loving fullness, therefore): “hear, my son, your father’s instruction” (1:8); “my son, if you receive my words” (2:1); “my son, do not forget my teaching” (3:1); “hear, O sons, a father’s instruction” (4:1); “my son, be attentive to my wisdom” (5:1); “my son, if you have become surety for your neighbor” (6:1); “my son, keep my words” (7:1).

Unlike Deuteronomy, in which an entire people is summoned to listen, in Proverbs listening becomes familiar, intimate: an attentive father bends over a son who needs to learn. Above all, the trembling love of a God who wants him as a “son” is revealed to man. Those seven appeals show the constancy of that benevolent will, the Father’s passionate desire to make known the beauty of his gift.

The importance of this listening is underlined at once by man’s need to keep silence: “the talkative man comes to ruin… the mouth of the fool is a danger… in much talking sin is not lacking… the prudent man keeps silent… he who speaks without thinking pierces like a sword… he who guards his mouth preserves his life… talkativeness brings only poverty… the mind of the righteous ponders before answering… even a fool, if he keeps silent, is thought wise… death and life are in the power of the tongue… the most precious thing is instructed lips…”

To listen, then, in order to become “skilled,” “sensible,” “prudent”… To know (19:27; 21:16; 22:17-18)…

Reading: PROVERBS 8 - 9:1-6

Important, then, is the welcoming of Wisdom. “Begotten” by God when the world had not yet been created. Present beside him as “master craftsman.” Each day of that eternity she was God’s “delight.” She herself rejoiced before God and… rejoiced in the whole creation.

And as Wisdom was God’s delight, we all, “sons of men,” were “his delight”! Happy this Wisdom, who possesses “life,” to whom “power belongs”; she is “understanding” itself and is pleased to give herself to kings, to magistrates, to rulers, that they may govern and teach with justice. She possesses “riches and honor,” prudence, knowledge, reflection, “well-being and equity.” Generous and loving to all who love her, she lets herself be found by those who seek her. Her mouth “proclaims the truth.”

She builds herself a “house… perfect, to invite the simple, those without sense, the hungry…”

In short, all of us, poor in these gifts!

To eat at her banquet will mean learning to be prudent, to know how to choose, to find discernment (19:8; 16:1.9; 21:2.31; 25:2; 30:8ff).

To become, through the gift of her understanding, knowers of the good, meditating and keeping the “memory” of history (29:18).

Peace will come as the fruit of keeping her teachings (19:2; 23:23; 24:3), and so:

– patience (14:29; 16:32) and also

– humility (15:33; 18:12; 22:4; 28:13.26).

Whoever listens to her, even if he falls, will rise again (24:16; 28:13-14); by his “discretion” (19:11; 17:9), he will find the paths of:

– reconciliation, even with enemies (16:7; 17:5; 24:17; 25:21);

– with riches, honoring the Lord (3:9.27; 21:13).

Whoever hates her loves death, whose fruits are:

– envy (14:30; 23:17; 24:1);

– anger (15:18; 20:3; 22:24; 25:28; 27:4; 30:33);

– laziness (15:19; 21:25);

– pride (16:18; 21:4; 30:20);

– greed (21:6; 23:4.10; 27:20.24; 28:8.20.22);

– presumption (15:22; 21:5; 25:6).

In these “fatherly” teachings is sown the “revelation” of God the Father, who wants the good of his children, who loves concord among them, who desires them to be brothers (3:29-30; 11:12 = do not kill; 3:27-28; 10:2; 11:1; 15:27; 28:8 = do not steal; 4:1; 12:11.17.22; 21:6 = do not bear false witness; 20:20 = honor your father and your mother; 2:16-19; 5:3-5.15-19; 6:23-29; 7:11-23 = do not commit impure acts); who above all desires that men regard him as the source of every good (3:5-12; 11:17; 20:22 = you shall have no other merciful God)!

PRAYER EXERCISE: read all the citations as divine instruction addressed to you. A little at a time…

• Reread EXODUS 20: the 10 commandments.

In the light of the invitations of the Book of Proverbs, do you agree that the “Decalogue” is a “word” of… love?

Or do you still think that God revealed himself in history only to give us orders of “do not” or, at any rate, “prohibitions”?

• How do you live that pressing invitation of God to meet Wisdom?

• What does it mean for you today to “listen” to Wisdom?

• Do you feel the need to be invited into that “perfect house” built by Wisdom?

From Mother Rosa: “The Gift of God” ch. IV

CELEBRATION NO. 3

“BLESSED ARE WE… WHAT PLEASES GOD HAS BEEN REVEALED TO US” (Bar 4:4)

(Gleaning from the Book of SIRACH)

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION

Israel is a people “instructed and wise” because, as the prophet Baruch recalls, God “searched out the whole way to wisdom and gave her to Israel his beloved. Afterwards she appeared on earth and lived among men” (Bar 3:37-38).

Sirach, too, feels the need to write “something about instruction and wisdom, so that those who love learning… may make even greater progress in living according to the law.”

“After devoting myself to it with much vigil and study”… we too, today, can glimpse in some sacred author a… fatherly invitation to welcome Wisdom, by him also described as… a person (15:1-10; 24).

“She comes from the Lord and is with him forever,” to reveal to us first of all that God alone is great (18:1-14; 43:27-33): the work of creation is his (1; 42:15-22; 17:1-15); only by grace is she known to man (11:4-6).

It is true, man cannot boast; he is poor (40:1-11), yet he is called to “beatitude” (14:1-2.20-27; 50:27-29), able to admire the works of God, not only in creation, but above all in the history of his “chosen ones” (44:1-15).

The welcoming of Wisdom, in fact, invites us to holiness, to exult in the praise of the holy and merciful God, who “grants joy of heart and… peace” (39:12-35; 50:22-24); who provides for all and who, on the day of eternity, will have all recognized as “good.” Each man has his task, his… “place” (38:24-34); but whoever “glories in the law of the Lord’s covenant… will never be forgotten” and “when he dies, he will already have done enough for himself” (39:1-11).

Reading: SIRACH 2

The author lets us know a new aspect of the revelation…

The man who “listens,” the man who is “prudent” and “instructed” in the ways of God; the man who has welcomed Wisdom must prepare himself for… temptation! He can go astray: because there is a time of… seduction! Eve, too, forgetting the “word of God” that had been announced to her: “of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die” (Gen 2:17), seduced, saw that tree…: “good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining wisdom” (Gen 3:6).

Glory will come, the wise man will certainly be “exalted,” but there is a path of… trial, of “painful vicissitudes.” From tribulation, in fact, the righteous will be saved. Paul too will testify: “afflicted in every way, but not crushed” (2 Cor 4:8).

The life of the righteous is humbled, but secure in the “arms” of the Lord.

CELEBRATION NO. 4

“THE LORD GAVE, THE LORD HAS TAKEN AWAY”

(Gleaning from the Book of Job)

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION

Sirach warned: “Prepare yourself for temptation!”

The Book of Job explains what “temptation” consists of and… that danger of “going astray in the time of seduction.”

This inspired book opens a window onto the drama of suffering and death: there is an enemy, an accuser who spies on the relationship between God and man, wants to interfere, to distract from listening, from welcoming divine wisdom, which, on the contrary, as we have seen, takes its delight in being with men. He is the “adversary” who appears in the history of humanity, to seduce and destroy the work of God: that image of his own with which man was created.

Out of envy, then, out of rage, out of hostility…

He appears at the beginning of creation (Gen 3); we do not know the why and the how of his rebellion against God…

Cunning, he enters into the lives of men and questions them with subtle trickery of words, casting suspicion on God’s real intentions.

In this book he attempts an even bigger stroke: he wants to seduce even God! To disillusion him of the esteem he has for Job, showing himself skeptical about the blessings that men can send up to God…

Reading: JOB 1

So God trusts man: he believes in that image and in that spirit with which he clothed him. He hopes in the beauty and intelligence of his creature: that he may “speak… well” of him, of his marvelous works.

On the other hand, man must reckon with this being who, on the contrary, speaks ill of man to God and casts serious doubt on God’s goodness before man…

Suffering, pain, loneliness, injustice and all evils seem not to be attributable to God, quite the contrary: they are the unleashing of the subtle and implacable hatred of “Satan,” who enjoys a special “permission” from the divine authority. A God, moreover, trusting in man’s patience. Above all attentive and desirous that, even in the darkness of trial, and left temporarily and within due limits in the hands of a ferocious enemy, man should not lose his confidence in him; almighty and merciful God, creator and good father of all creatures.

A truly incomprehensible magnanimity, the divine one, which lets this rebel “roam” the whole earth, apparently at liberty and even “in the midst” of the angels, who, for their part, also seem to accept his company benignly; hateful enemy of men who, precisely, “prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour” (1 Pet 5:8).

Job will not understand this… stripping of his. He will come to curse his life: the suffering is too great! (3) He will want to die (6:1-10). But even in the oppression and weariness of a tormented life, he cries out… against God! (7)

A cry, a reproach, a protest, to the One who should understand him, whom deep down he continues to esteem, refusing to accept, as his friends would have him believe, that he has sinned: “God does not reject the blameless… if you are pure, from now on he will watch over you” (8), so they reproach him.

They think he has sins of omission. But like a “violent wind,” Job finds no peace: “Why are you my adversary, God?… Why did you bring me out of the womb? Would that I had died!” (10:2.18).

This burning “talkativeness” offends the hypocritical religiosity of his friends: “Do you think you can fathom the depths of God?” (11)

Job claims to have understanding. He knows God’s limitless power; there is no need to present oneself as… “defenders of God”!

He keeps on speaking, complaining, to “defend his conduct before him.”

Most tender, most heartfelt, that protest: “Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?” Job, deep down, appeals to him (12; 13:13; - 14:6).

He feels nostalgia for his former condition… (29:1-10) and laments his present one (30:1.9-23); he continues to defend his conduct, which is… according to justice (31:1-8.13-23.35-37).

Riches are vanity (5:9); even wisdom: it is useless (7:16-17.20)!

RETREAT NO. 3

JESUS SPOKE OF THE KINGDOM OF GOD

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION:

If the evangelists’ testimonies on the death-resurrection of Jesus are important (note how Luke opens his gospel declaring that he “decided to investigate everything accurately from the very beginning… the events that have taken place” in the land of Jesus: Lk 1:1-4 and how John, on the other hand, closes his by protesting his truthful witness to… “these things,” that is, to what he has written about the life and work of Jesus: Jn 21:24-25), equally compelling are the testimonies of the Book of Acts on the conversion of Paul (note here too the care of Luke, who moreover shared with Paul in good part the ministry of evangelization, in reminding us, at the beginning of the book, of the work of Jesus concluded, after his passion and his death, with… his showing himself alive, appearing for 40 days and then being taken up into heaven).

After having celebrated, last time, Paul’s testimony before King Agrippa, it will be good to listen to the account the evangelist gives of the apostle’s conversion and then the testimony that he himself will give to the Jews.

Reading: ACTS 9:1-30 and 22

You have before you the meeting of Jesus with Paul. You surely remember the one Jesus had with the apostles and the women, narrated by the evangelists. You will also have noticed, in the letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor 15:5-9), how Paul speaks of various “appearances” of the risen Jesus: to Cephas, to the “twelve,” to James, to all the apostles (probably others besides the Twelve…), finally also to him (and Paul considers himself the “least” among those chosen for this mission, precisely because of his earlier persecutions which, instead of making the Church grow, had made her suffer).

But it is interesting to note how Paul recalls an appearance of Jesus that others do not recount: to “more than 500 brothers at one time.” Perhaps it took place in a Eucharistic celebration, or in any case in an assembly of prayer. Perhaps in a vigil. A great assembly of brothers. Probably among the first converted by the testimony of Peter and the others, right after Pentecost: Luke in fact recalls that “about 3000 persons were added to them” who were baptized that day. All people who already knew Jesus, had heard him preach, who had probably also been witnesses of his miracles or healings, but who that Friday before Pilate, frightened by the reprisals of the Jewish police, collaborators of the Roman one and incited to testify against Jesus… had shouted that terrible “crucify him!” (Mt 27:20; Mk 15:11; Lk 23:13). Now, repentant, they were part of that first Christian community of Jerusalem: “listening to the teaching of the apostles, in fraternal union, in the breaking of the bread and in prayers” (Acts 2:42-48). Probably in one of these gatherings, under the guidance of some apostle, this “appearance” mentioned by Paul had taken place: truly consoling! And Paul, to confirm what he knows, hastens to declare: “most of them are still alive.” It is possible, then, to consult them, to obtain from them themselves, eyewitnesses, the certainty of what the apostles, and now Paul too, are preaching.

Jesus is, in short, confirming his community in the faith it must profess: its Master and Lord who was crucified is alive! Many have seen him and will see him. Very many others will know him through the proclamation that the apostles will make of him. Remember what Jesus says to Thomas: “blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe!” (Jn 20:29).

As John himself affirms: the gospels were written precisely to arouse faith in Jesus in those who, though not present at his appearances, can meet him in his word… witnessed to by the evangelists. (Jn 20:31).

“THEY WILL SEE SOMETHING NEVER TOLD TO THEM…”

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION:

“…and they will understand what they had never heard” (Is 52:15).

By now you will have understood the importance and that insistence which Moses and the prophets of Israel urged on the whole people, and not only them, but the generations to come, to “listen,” that is, to keep in the memory of the nation that truly never-told event: the liberation from Egypt, the Passover of Yahweh!…

“Hear, O Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.” One and alone, certainly, in that way of his acting: “for he has triumphed gloriously; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Ex 15).

This “song” has run through the whole history of a people. Even in times of sorrow, Israel’s hope was sustained by the memory of that “event,” and the prophets could venture the announcement of a… new exodus: “I am the Lord, who made all things, who stretched out the heavens alone, who spread out the earth; who was with me?… I say of Jerusalem: She shall be inhabited, and of the cities of Judah: They shall be rebuilt… and of the Temple: Your foundation shall be laid” (Is 44:24-28); “I, I am the Lord, and besides me there is no savior… Do not remember the former things… Behold, I am doing a new thing: I will make a way in the wilderness” (Is 43:11-21). This song, rooted in the heart of those people, is the force that animates them, that makes them exult: “Who is like you, majestic in holiness?… In your favor you led the people whom you redeemed, you guided them to your holy abode.”

Israel cannot, must not forget how much it has been loved!

To us too remains the inheritance of this “song in honor of the Lord.” Even more wondrous and majestic is his triumph: he has destroyed sin and death!…

We cannot forget the love revealed to us by the Servant of God, the Lord Jesus!

Reading: ROMANS 10

As a good… doctor of the Law and become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven, Paul “knows how to bring out of his treasure what is new and what is old” (Mt 13:52); he knows, that is, how to illuminate the prophecies of the past with the splendor of the fulfillment accomplished by Jesus. His heart, softened by the mercy obtained, now desires the conversion of his people. He has understood the profound dignity of Israel, of being the repository of the divine promises: the adoption as children, the glory, the covenants, the worship, the patriarchs… (cf. Rom 9:4-5) As he himself once was, so now they: zealous for God… “but not according to knowledge.” For them Paul sends up his prayer; salvation lies in welcoming the gift of that journey of… centuries, the fruit of so many expectations. How much that people suffered to see a land… not only material! To live a justice that would not be only a human effort or mere outward attitudes. How much the prophets let them hope for a… new covenant, accomplished by God alone (…his justice!); rooted and sealed in man’s very heart! Another great wonder of Yahweh, another “event” to… be told to future generations.

The justice that Israel sought was too… human. “The one who does these things will live by them” (Gal 3:12). But man had shown himself incapable of observing it. The law is holy; man, weakened by sin, could only… admire its sublimity!

This is what Paul has experienced. Man’s impossibility of saving himself: it is necessary to welcome with trust what God has prepared: that Son who became a “curse” (Gal 3:13) or was treated as “sin” (2 Cor 5:21) on our behalf, and then that cry of man: “how to go up to heaven,” how to please God? He finds the answer: Christ came down to earth to accomplish redemption, to give us a way, an example, Peter told us; or: “who will descend into the abyss,” who can enter into death, freely, without fear?… Likewise he finds him, Jesus, present and active to destroy the nightmare: Christ who rises and brings the message: “peace to you!”

Behold, for Paul the “word” of preaching is the Easter event of Jesus. If you confess what you have received: that Jesus is now the Lord of victory, of life, and you truly believe that he is risen, you will be saved. Because you will be able to call upon the one who died for you and lives for you; to help you, to be near you. Because he, loving you from always, sent his own to announce to you a thing that had never been told to you and to make you understand what you had never heard. Now, knowing, you can believe, that is, put your trust in so many witnesses so as not to be disappointed, when, calling upon a Lord rich towards all, you too will be able to taste how good Jesus is and sing with all: “the Lord is my strength and my song!”

INTRODUCTION TO THE CELEBRATION:

John testified to us, in the 13th celebration, that, with the apostles, he heard, saw, contemplated, touched the… “Word of life.” And what they “saw and heard” they can “announce” to us.

This proclamation therefore has as its content a concrete person: Jesus (John calls him: the Word… become “flesh”). In the prologue of his gospel, in fact, the Word sketched by the apostle-evangelist is God himself (1:1); through him everything came into existence (1:3). Not only that, but the “Word became flesh” (1:14). That is: God became man. God dwelt in Jesus. The glory of which they were “spectators” is what was revealed to them, precisely, by the Son who was “at the Father’s side” (1:18). A gift to which we men had no right at all!

Jesus is a living reality: who continues to give himself; John, in fact, had added: “our communion is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.”

The apostles are aware, that is, of announcing not only Jesus, his life, his paschal event of death and resurrection, but a “remaining” of Jesus with them or, better, of their being… “assumed,” almost, or inserted into the very life of relationship that the Son has with the Father and which, with his glorified humanity, he communicates to them incessantly. The love that Jesus had testified to his own in his earthly life, he manifests all the more now in guiding them in this mission of proclamation and witness to the whole world!

Proclamation of an event, that of Jesus, and witness to their new way of living: communion with the inner life of relationship between the Father and the Son.

It was what the “twelve” had affirmed about their particular charism: “prayer” and the ministry of the “word” (Acts 6:2-4). Prayer understood, precisely, as a life of communion with God. Moreover, both Matthew 28:20: “I am with you always…”; and Mark 16:20: “the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word with signs”; and Luke 24:49: “I will send upon you what my Father promised…”, that is, the Holy Spirit, confirm this real and effective presence, in the work of evangelization, of Jesus himself: it is he who works; it is he who continually pours out the Spirit for the “conversion” and the “forgiveness of sins” of all men (Lk 24:47).

John too closes his gospel with a clear command of the Risen One to Peter, head of the Church, the one who must “shepherd” Jesus’ flock: “Follow me!” It is Jesus alone who guides the Church and works in her through his own who… follow him (see for example Gal 2:8.20).

But Paul too, in the last celebration, affirmed that “preaching is accomplished by the word of Christ.” That is, it is he, Jesus, who, acting in communion with his own, working with them, continually giving his Spirit of love, comforting them, inspiring in them confidence and peace, forgiving them and lifting them from their frailties, makes them capable of a witness that surpasses human strength and capacities. The object of preaching is therefore Jesus himself risen, who becomes a present reality for those who listen. The apostles, in fact, do not proclaim their own personal opinions…

Reading: 1 PETER 1

The very beginning shows us the effective call brought about by the spirit of Jesus, who asks for obedience: “Follow me!” He, in fact, saved us by his sacrifice, baptizing us in his blood.

The new birth to which we have been called is the work of the resurrection of Jesus, of his victory over our death. The prophets too, guided by the Spirit of Jesus who was at work in them, prepared the preaching of the apostles: the fulfillment of all God’s promises, of that Jesus who now guides the Church in preaching the victorious event of his passage from death to the life of heaven, with all humanity healed from the wounds of sin and from the fear of death.

But even more clearly Peter closes the chapter saying: you have been “born anew, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, that is, through the living and abiding word of God.”

“Word,” therefore, which is not only the expression of concepts or feelings, but an event that becomes actual, the effective passage of a divine action that recreates, regenerates; that brings about a new reality in the one who listens and welcomes and believes!

Paul has no doubt in affirming that apostolic preaching, besides being accomplished by the will of Christ who sends his own, works wonders thanks to the outpouring of the Spirit (Gal 3:1-5; 1 Thess 2:13). He insists on saying that the welcoming of this “word” is the welcoming of a divine event.

RETREAT NO. 4

After so many testimonies, you have been invited to believe in the resurrection of Jesus. There is no Christianity without this fact. The proclamation, the preaching of this event, is affirmed with insistence and firmness by people who assure us they were sent by Jesus himself alive. What they narrate is not their own doctrine; it is not their ideologies; they do not belong to theological or rabbinic schools; they do not defend opinions or hypotheses; they are not “blinded by pride” or “morbidly craving for controversy and quarrels over words” (1 Tim 6:4); they do not “pay attention to Jewish myths or to commandments of people who turn away from the truth” (Titus 1:14), nor “to deceitful spirits and demonic doctrines” (1 Tim 4:1)…In short, what they affirm cannot be argued with. They know it is not by their own will that they exercise this ministry: they obey a mandate and cannot but obey (Acts 4:5-20): “you are my friends if you do what I command you” (Jn 15:14).

They testify with assurance to the mandate Jesus holds to give forgiveness and the Spirit. They know they have a “power” given to them (Mt 28:18-20) to teach, instruct, heal, give life, arousing faith with their Easter proclamation. With that immortal, living and eternal “word” (1 Pet 1:23).

This is now the “wisdom” of men “born from above,” of a wind and a fire whose voice they have recognized…they knew where it came from, but not where it would send them (cf. Jn 3:7-8).

Men “regarded as impostors, and yet true; as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold we live; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything” (cf. 2 Cor 6:8-10).

Chosen for this ministry, then, not because they were learned or capable or powerful or noble, quite the contrary…(1 Cor 1:26) “earthen vessels,” but so that in them might appear the “extraordinary power that comes from God and not from them” (cf. 2 Cor 4:7).

Chosen, yes…elected for a divine mission. So that no one may boast. Only Christ has conquered, he…exalted. He alone the “Living One” (Rev 1:17-18)!

Because he alone has loved! And only his love, his life, attract, convert, save. He alone for all: “wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, redemption” (1 Cor 1:30).

You can meditate on the election of great biblical figures who in some way anticipated the mission of Jesus. You can realize how they too…poor “earthen vessels”!

MOSES. Scripture is very sober about his youthful life. Raised by Pharaoh’s daughter…“he became her son.” Then “when he had grown up, he went out to his people and saw their forced labor.” To defend them, he kills an Egyptian…Then?

Moses “was afraid” and “fled from Pharaoh.” His capacity?…To become “an alien residing in a foreign land”! (Ex 2:10-22).

Only “grace” will make of this man a…leader, a teacher, a lawgiver. Because God will be with him. God “will stretch out his hand and strike Egypt” (Ex 3:20), “with an outstretched arm he will free Israel from slavery” (Ex 6:6-7).

DAVID, loved by God from childhood, chosen as king. Courageous in defending “the armies of the living God” whom Goliath insulted (1 Sam 17:32-36). Faithful and devoted to Saul, who nonetheless will pursue him to death, he will save Saul’s life twice, forgiving him (1 Sam 24:1-16; 26). Beautiful is the funeral elegy with which he will exalt Saul and Jonathan, killed by the Philistines (2 Sam 1:17-27).

And yet he too will experience his own weakness, will know his sin: he will be an adulterer and a murderer! (2 Sam 11)

He will ask for a “clean heart,” a “steadfast spirit”; he will invoke that “joy of being saved” in order to “teach – he too a repentant sinner – transgressors the ways of divine mercy” (Ps 51).

PETER will deny three times that he knows Jesus, he who before was ready to go with the master to prison and to death. The prayer of Jesus will save him (Lk 22:31-34.61-62).

But the great ELIJAH too will have his moment of bewilderment and fear: he will flee from his mission. Only that mysterious bread and the sound of a gentle breeze…will save him (1 Kgs 19:1-14).

So JOHN THE BAPTIST, the strong “voice” who prepared the people to welcome the Messiah, baptizing Jesus, will know in prison the hour of darkness, the doubt, the anguish of having failed in his mission (Mt 11:1-6).

And how many times will ABRAHAM doubt on his journey? (Gen 15:1-5) And how great the frailty experienced by ISAIAH: “a man of unclean lips, lost”? (Is 6:5) By JEREMIAH, who curses the day of his birth, because he is forced to live amid “toil and sorrow”? (Jer 20:7-18) A messenger of Satan will strike PAUL, that he may learn to trust solely in God’s “grace”! (2 Cor 12:7-9).

Of the fact that we are bound in solidarity with Adam and therefore there are no…individual salvations?

That the pride, the arrogance and the contempt for the “word” of God, which caused the original disobedience, must be purified by man’s return to humility, to simplicity, to patience, to trusting abandonment?

Rom 11:33), to the…possession of his divine nature! To the gift of the Spirit of the Only-Begotten Son, who now provokes that cry of exultation: “Abba, Father!”

One hears, in that insistence on Christ in you (present, moreover, in other passages of other letters…) or on the Spirit who dwells in you, the echo of the grace received at Damascus… That event marked Paul’s life: everything now is considered “loss.” Abysmal the difference between the life lived in the “flesh” (without knowledge of Christ) and the “new” one in the Spirit (guided by Christ).

He can allow himself to affirm: “if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him!”

At this point it is important to compare, once again: Acts 9:1–30; Phil 3:7-16; Eph 1:15-23 with Rom 8:1-17:

Try to describe the action of the Holy Spirit; his influence in the life of the Church, but not only, in the journey of every man; his effectiveness; his guidance; the power to transfigure the creature; his gifts…

- What experience do you have of Him?

- What do you read of Him in everyday life? Do you see “signs” of his presence in the people around you?

CONCLUSIONS

Here ends this third little volume, in the hope that it has been of help on the spiritual journey of the brothers of the Movement. It had to have an…end, as, after all, do all our human realities!

The “Divine Office” (prayer or, better, the celebration of Lauds and Vespers, that is…), on the other hand, has no end. It is a “sacred duty” (precisely: a “divine office”!) that the Church entrusts to her children, so that they may not only learn to pray, but above all so that they may make present, by invocation or thanksgiving…“without ceasing” (cf. 1 Thess 5:17), “with all kinds,” that is, “of prayers and supplications in the Spirit” (Eph 6:18), the mercy and benevolence of God.

“To celebrate” is, in fact: to cry out for help, to seek, to stretch out our hands, without growing weary, to Him who alone can free us from every oppression: “Hear, O holy Father, the voice of the faithful… Break our chains, heal our wounds, forgive our sins. Without you we are submerged in a deep whirlpool of sins and darkness,” so goes a Tuesday “hymn.”

In every “celebration” we “remember” God, we “meditate” on his saving interventions, we “think again” on days past… We “reflect”: the inspired “words” question us, open us to hope: “God cannot reject us forever, nor make his love for each of us cease,” so the psalmist (cf. Ps 77).

Everything has an end or fulfillment, but “celebrating” the wonderful works of God is a “task” that knows no end! Indeed: “from generation to generation the Almighty extends his mercy to those who fear him,” Mary will sing in her…“office”!

And so Zechariah: the “tender mercy of God” will come to visit us to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death (cf. Lk 1:46-55. 68-79).

This light that comes from on high we must always invoke, “keeping alert with all perseverance to this end.” What do we sing in the “Gloria” of the “Eucharistic celebration”? “We worship you, Lord, we bless you, we adore you, we give you thanks for your great glory”!

We will never be able to exhaust, therefore, the knowledge of that glory which is the divine life in which He has wished to make us sharers. Not even in heaven will we finish celebrating the praise and the hymn of blessing and thanksgiving for this extraordinary grace. So: our certainty is in Him who “lives and reigns forever and ever” and lives in us so that our joy now and always may be full!
